skill.name: database-migration-helper
skill.description: Guides creation of database migration files for common ORMs while matching project naming, rollback, and safety conventions.
skill.summary: Create convention-aligned database migrations with rollback and testing guidance.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, ORM file names, migration examples, and type-only JSDoc imports. Confirmed risk is limited to Bash-enabled instructions that run package managers or framework CLIs to generate migrations. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Migration generator commands can execute project code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx, npm, alembic, python manage.py, or rails commands. Prefer manual file generation for untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Migration commands can target the wrong database environment.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions to verify the active environment, database URL, backups, and staging status before executing any migration command.

remediation.issue: Package-manager commands can run unreviewed local or downloaded code.
remediation.suggestion: Review package manifests and lockfiles before using npx or npm-based migration generators. Prefer pinned project-local tooling when available.

content.value_statement: Database migrations can break applications when file names, rollback logic, or ORM conventions are wrong. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create convention-aligned migrations with rollback guidance.
actual_capabilities: Detects common migration tools from project files and directory structure.
Reviews existing migrations for naming, timestamps, and up/down patterns.
Generates migration files for Prisma, Sequelize, Knex, TypeORM, Alembic, Django, and Rails.
Adds rollback, index, foreign key, and data safety guidance when supported.
Suggests testing steps for development, staging, and rollback validation.
limitations: Does not guarantee generated migrations are safe for production data.
May need database-specific review for locking, online DDL, and large-table changes.
Some ORM generators require Bash commands and user approval.
Does not replace DBA review for destructive or high-volume migrations.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Table
use_cases.description: Create a new table with primary keys, timestamps, indexes, and rollback steps that match the existing ORM convention.

use_cases.title: Standardize ORM Migrations
use_cases.description: Review existing migration patterns and create new files that follow team naming, directory, and rollback practices.

use_cases.title: Plan Safer Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Identify data loss, locking, rollback, and staging checks before applying table changes or index updates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner migration for a small schema change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration to add a nullable phone field to users. Detect the ORM first, follow existing naming, and include rollback guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add an Indexed Relationship
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration with a foreign key and index.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration that adds an account relationship to projects. Include the foreign key, index, rollback, and any data safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Backfill Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration that changes schema and existing data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration that adds order_status, backfills existing orders, and removes the old active flag. Separate schema and data steps when appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced safety review before a high-risk deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned migration for rollback gaps, table locks, data loss, and deployment order. Suggest safer alternatives for large tables.

output_examples.input: Add a unique email index to users in a Knex project.
output: Detected Knex from the project configuration and existing migrations.
Prepared a timestamped migration name that matches local naming patterns.
Included an apply step, rollback step, unique index note, and development test checklist.

output_examples.input: Create an Alembic migration for order status.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify the Alembic versions directory, create a revision-style migration, add upgrade and downgrade steps, and warn about backfilling existing rows.

output_examples.input: Check whether a planned column removal is safe.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag data loss risk, suggest a deprecation period, confirm dependent application code, and recommend backup and rollback validation.

best_practices: Review generated SQL and ORM behavior before applying production migrations.
Test both apply and rollback paths against realistic development or staging data.
Keep schema and data migrations separate unless the project convention requires otherwise.
anti_patterns: Running migration commands against production without confirming the active environment.
Combining unrelated table changes, data backfills, and index rebuilds in one migration.
Dropping columns or data before application code and backups are ready.

faq.question: Which migration tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma, Sequelize, Knex, TypeORM, Alembic, Django, Rails, Flyway, Liquibase, and similar migration layouts.

faq.question: Can it run migration generator commands?
faq.answer: Yes, but commands such as npx, npm, python manage.py, and rails should require user confirmation before execution.

faq.question: Does it create rollback logic?
faq.answer: It includes down, downgrade, rollback, or reversible change guidance when the selected ORM supports it.

faq.question: Can it handle data migrations?
faq.answer: It can plan data migrations and recommend batching, but high-volume backfills still need careful database review.

faq.question: Will it guarantee production safety?
faq.answer: No. Production migrations require staging tests, backups, environment checks, and review of locking or data loss risks.

faq.question: How should I use it in an unfamiliar repository?
faq.answer: Ask it to inspect conventions first, generate files manually where possible, and avoid running commands until you approve them.
